title: Polynomial-time preimage closure
statement: Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $g$ be a polynomial-time computable function from binary strings to binary strings. Then the language $\{x:g(x)\in V\}$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
replaced: Let $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time, and let $g : \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ be polynomial-time computable (computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then the preimage $g^{-1}(V) = \{x \in \{0,1\}^* : g(x) \in V\}$ also belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
